text:
ashley: Quick follow-up from the routing-policy RFC — I'm worried our current invalidation semantics for geo-weighted caches will create subtle latency cliffs during rollouts. TL;DR: when a policy switch changes region weights, cached route decisions can persist and cause hot traffic to stay pinned to a depleted region for minutes. We need a concrete plan for invalidation + graceful drain.

samir: yup saw this in the sim yesterday. two obvious levers: (1) conservative TTLs on cache entries after a policy update, or (2) propagate a policy-change event that marks affected keys as stale. tradeoff is more churn vs temporary extra latency from recomputes.

jun: sidecar vs library matters here. if policy runtime is a sidecar we can push an async invalidation event to the local sidecar and shadow-evict entries quickly. library-first means cross-service API surface for invalidation which is harder to coordinate.

margo: i'm leaning toward sidecar + hybrid invalidation. plan: on policy-change, compute a minimal impacted-key fingerprint set (via the policy compiler), send a fanout to affected sidecars with a version stamp, and let sidecars either immediately evict or mark as stale-per-probe. this keeps the control plane light. also add a safety TTL backstop.

ashley: sounds reasonable. two follow-ups: (a) compiler needs to export the fingerprint set — is that heavy? (b) what's our signal for immediate evict vs mark-stale?

samir: compiler shouldn't be heavy if we do it at policy-compile time (not per-decision). we can produce a compact Bloom-ish set keyed by route fingerprint. size should be modest. for evict vs stale, use traffic heat: if a route has QPS > threshold then mark-stale (triggers local probe/fetch), else lazy TTL.

jun: runtime concern: sidecar memory pressure if many tenants, plus network fanout storm. add rate-limited invalidation and exponential backoff per sidecar. also ensure invalidation is idempotent with version numbers.

margo: agreed. add per-tenant quota for invalidation traffic, and a fallback policy: when invalidation requests are dropped, targeted sidecars fall back to a safe route variant (e.g., capacity-aware low-weight region) instead of leaving stale routes.

ashley: ops question — how do we test this without impacting prod? we need sim + shadow rollout plan.

samir: simulation steps: (1) policy compile to fingerprint set, (2) synthetic traffic replay with varying QPS skews, (3) trigger invalidation fanout and measure mean-time-to-stable-route and tail latency. include region outage spikes. i can wire this into the policy preflight harness.

margo: also add an observability contract: invalidation events must emit telemetry: policy_id, affected_shards_estimate, per-sidecar ack/nack, and time-to-evict. Dashboard + canary alerts if >X% didn't ack within Ys.

jun: API surface we need documented: 
```
POST /policy/v1/invalidate
{ "policy_id": "p-2026-23", "version": "v13", "fingerprint_batch_url": "s3://.../bloom-000" }
```
sidecar must accept versioned invalidations and return {accepted:true, queued:false|true}.

ashley: love the API. final thing: rollout strategy. propose canary on 1% of tenants with active probing enabled, run for 15m, then 10% for 30m, then ramp. abort if tail latency > 99p baseline + 50ms or if >0.5% of invalidations are nacks.

infra-bot: deploy-note: policy-compiler PR #482 merged. preflight sim job queued: job/route-inval-sim-3312345678. logs: https://ci.redwood.example/run/3312345678 

samir: I'll own the sim wiring and the metric set. jun can you own sidecar changes (idempotent invalidation handling + rate limit)? margo you own observability + dashboard. ashley will coordinate rollout with SRE.

ashley: agreed. thanks! i'll draft the follow-up RFC appendix with the API and rollout plan and link the sim checklist. :thumbsup:
